clue.text: Mean injunction after non-U plenitude of drink

indicators.note: after puts the piece from injunction behind the trimmed drink piece
non- in front of U says the letter U is taken out of what follows

parts.note: a skinful is as much drink as one can hold
the letter U itself, as in the old U and non-U class labels
read as IN plus junction, the T of a T-junction

explanation.surface: A stingy order issued after a working-class drinking bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-U' is the old British label for speech or habits not of the upper class, here read literally as dropping the letter. 'injunction' looks like a court order but splits as IN + T, the shape of a T-junction.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser is a mean person, the stock image of the tight-fisted.

clue.text: Like Gordius, who once kept wicket for England?

definitions.text: Like Gordius, who once kept wicket for England?

parts.words: Like Gordius, who once kept wicket for England
parts.note: Gordius is the setter, named after the king of the tangled Gordian knot; Alan Knott kept wicket for England, so Knott-like too

explanation.walkthrough: Alan Knott was England's wicketkeeper in the 1970s; a wicketkeeper is the cricket fielder behind the stumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tangled or puzzling, as the Gordian knot was, is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Drains are directed to the lowest points

indicators.note: directed, as in sent another way, has the letters of drains set in a new order

explanation.surface: Drainage is channelled down to the lowest ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A nadir is the bottom-most point of anything, the opposite of a zenith.

clue.text: Not "Early" nor "County" but dignified!

parts.note: earl and count give Earl-y and Count-y; a third title, a peer of the realm, does the same with -ly

explanation.surface: Not early nor county, but dignified!
explanation.definitionFit: Behaving like a noble peer means having a stately, haughty dignity.

clue.text: He's put up, but setter's a long time without rising

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the long time goes round the setter's piece
in a down clue rising means read from the bottom up

parts.note: an eon is an age
the setter speaking of what is his: mine

explanation.surface: Someone is proposed, but the setter has been a long time getting up.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate put up for election or office is a nominated person.

clue.text: Extreme policy — state impulse to light …

indicators.note: extreme letters are those at each end of the word policy

parts.note: Romania is a European country, a state

explanation.surface: A radical policy, as a nation's urge to set things alight.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs into the next clue; it is part of the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyromania is a compulsive urge to start fires, an impulse to set things alight.

clue.text: … thereby one cop to cover seat

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: cover means the officer goes round the seat

parts.note: PC, police constable
a sofa is a seat
taken as written

explanation.surface: Thus a policeman is to sit over a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means by that very fact, so thereby.

clue.text: Additional item that could be charged

definitions.meaning: an extra item such as a handbag added to an outfit
an accomplice in a crime, liable to a criminal charge

explanation.definitionFit: An extra add-on item is an accessory, and so is an accomplice, who may be charged in court.

clue.text: Hardly able to see setter's round illustration

parts.note: the setter speaking of his own: my
a round shape, the letter O
pic is short for picture

explanation.surface: The setter's round picture is hard to make out.
explanation.definitionFit: Short-sighted people cannot see distant things clearly.

clue.text: Officer farmed out nursery item

parts.note: Col, short for colonel, an army officer

indicators.note: out as in disordered, so farmed is rearranged

explanation.surface: A commander leased out a piece of kit for the nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nursery' is the plant kind, not the children's.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold frame is a glass box used in plant nurseries to shelter seedlings.

clue.text: Runner holds back toy animal

indicators.note: holds means the runner goes around the other piece

parts.note: Sebastian Coe, the British middle-distance runner

indicators.note: back means the word toy is read in reverse

explanation.surface: An athlete hangs on to a returned plaything animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The coyote is a wild dog of North America, an animal.

clue.text: Flier gets overtime, which is alarming

indicators.note: gets means the bird takes in the extra piece

parts.note: a starling is a bird, a flier
extra time, abbreviated T for time

explanation.surface: A pilot is paid overtime, which is shocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Startling things give one a sudden fright, so they are alarming.

clue.text: Pester to the point girl retreats

indicators.note: retreats means the girl's name goes backwards

parts.note: Sarah is a girl's name
S, south, a compass point

explanation.surface: A girl backs away from a man who annoys her to the point.
explanation.definitionFit: To harass is to annoy persistently, as pestering does.

clue.text: Someone once contrived to emulate 1

indicators.note: contrived means put together artfully, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: split as some plus one, and one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone once schemed to copy the mean man at 1 across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Someone' gives SOME plus I (one), and these join ONCE as the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Imitating a miser means cutting spending, being thrifty.

clue.text: Exit duty?

parts.note: exit as death and duty as a toll, a fee; the phrase reads as a tax on leaving

explanation.definitionFit: The number of people killed in a disaster is its count of fatalities.

clue.text: Repulsive scheme to turn to dust

indicators.note: scheme as a verb, to plot, so the letters of repulsive are rearranged

explanation.surface: A disgusting plan to reduce something to powder.
explanation.definitionFit: To grind something down to powder is to pulverise it.

clue.text: Complimentary without right to payment

indicators.note: without means the letter for right is dropped

parts.note: complimentary tickets are free
R, short for right

explanation.surface: Something given free is not entitled to be paid for.
explanation.definitionFit: A fee is a charge or sum paid for a service.

clue.text: Article in paper about obesity?

indicators.note: in means the article sits inside the paper

parts.note: FT, the Financial Times newspaper
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper feature about being overweight.
explanation.definitionFit: Obesity is excess body tissue, the stuff of being overweight.

clue.text: Incite and one gets laid

explanation.definitionFit: To egg someone on is to urge them, and hens lay eggs.

clue.text: Pause as a cure for breakdown

indicators.note: breakdown says the letters of as a cure are broken up and remade

explanation.surface: Taking a rest as a cure for a nervous breakdown.
explanation.definitionFit: In poetry a caesura is a break in the middle of a line.

clue.text: Brilliance of a good surgeon?

parts.note: G, short for good
Joseph Lister, the pioneer of antiseptic surgery

explanation.surface: The genius of a fine surgeon.
explanation.definitionFit: Glister is an old word for glitter, a sparkling brilliance.

clue.text: Refrain from turning a weapon

indicators.note: turning means the gun word is read backwards

parts.note: gat is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: Avoid swinging round a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag can be a repeated line or chorus, as a refrain is.

clue.text: Egyptian deity — one with a strong nose

parts.note: Ammon, or Amun, the Egyptian god
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An Egyptian god, one with a powerful sense of smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammonia is famous for its pungent smell, a strong bouquet in the wine sense of nose.

clue.text: It's natural — alter this and you get something else

parts.words: alter this and you get something else
parts.note: put alter in front of the word and it becomes a word meaning something else, another option

explanation.surface: It's innate; change it and you have something different.
explanation.definitionFit: Native qualities are inborn, so natural.

clue.text: Leading lady in seafront but it won't get her a tan

definitions.text: it won't get her a tan

indicators.note: in means the lady's initial goes inside the seafront word

parts.note: the beach by the sea

indicators.note: leading picks the first letter of lady

explanation.surface: A star actress on the beach finds it doesn't bronze her.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleach whitens rather than darkens, the opposite of tanning.

clue.text: Goes across the Channel with lusty sound and is appreciated

parts.note: va is French for goes, in France across the English Channel

indicators.note: sound says that the word for lusty is heard, not spelt

parts.note: lewd means lustful

explanation.surface: Someone crosses to France, makes lusty noises and is liked.
explanation.definitionFit: Something valued is prized or held dear.

clue.text: Noose said to change at Bow

indicators.note: said means the word for change is spoken
Bow in East London is Cockney territory, where an H is dropped from speech

parts.note: to alter is to change

explanation.surface: A rope said to be swapped at Bow.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys famously drop their aitches, so the halter is said 'alter there; Bow is a district of East London, the Cockney heartland.
explanation.definitionFit: A halter is a rope with a loop, as a noose is.

clue.text: Girl in smart outfit may be suspicious

indicators.note: in places the girl inside the rearranged letters
outfit taken as a verb, so the letters of smart are refitted

parts.note: Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A woman in a stylish outfit may raise doubts.
explanation.definitionFit: To smell a rat is an idiom for suspecting foul play.

clue.text: Victor was no spring chicken

definitions.meaning: no longer young, of ripe years

explanation.definitionFit: Victor Mature was a Hollywood actor, and a mature person is no longer young.

clue.text: In 17 down you reportedly have consumed to turn to folly

parts.note: taken as written
the solution to the clue at 17 down

indicators.note: reportedly means the word you is as it is heard

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like U
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: At the cross-reference you are said to have eaten to grow foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: To infatuate is to inspire a foolish passion, making someone act with folly.

clue.text: Drop in the ocean and mountains turn quiet

indicators.note: turn means the range's name is read backwards

parts.note: the Alps are mountains
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A tiny amount in the sea, and the hills fall silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A splash is a small dash of liquid dropped into something.

clue.text: In cramped condition heartless Henry is an insensitive type

indicators.note: in places Henry's ends inside the reworked letters
condition as a verb, to treat, so the letters of cramped are worked over
heartless removes the inside of Henry, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: In a cramped state, cold-hearted Henry is a thick-skinned type.
explanation.definitionFit: A pachyderm is a thick-skinned animal, so a person impervious to criticism.
